name: nouride-wa-bridge
description: WhatsApp bridge for Nouride — its own module, speaking newline-delimited JSON to a host that compiles it in or reaches it over a WebSocket.
comment: Deliberately NOT a member of the root workspace: `@whiskeysockets/baileys` is
GPL-3.0 and must never land in the engine's node_modules. Install it here, on
its own:  cd plugins/wa-bridge && bun install
This package shares no code with the rest of the repo — the wire protocol in
src/protocol.ts is the entire interface, hand-copied from
packages/shared/src/types/bridge.ts and checked by the `hello` version field.
`libsignal` is aliased to a local shim that forwards to `whatsapp-rust-bridge` (MIT).
`overrides.libsignal` points the npm package of that name at a local shim which
forwards to `whatsapp-rust-bridge` (MIT). The real package is GPL-3.0 and is the only
reason a binary carrying this bridge is a combined work — Baileys itself is MIT.
An `overrides` entry rather than a plain dependency alias: Baileys depends on
`libsignal` itself, so bun installs a second copy under its own node_modules and a
root alias never reaches it.
See docs/rfc/PLAN_REPLACE_LIBSIGNAL.md in the parent repository.
`file:` COPIES the directory at install time, so an edit to the shim does not reach a
build until `bun install` runs again. That cost three deploys to a live box: the tests
imported the shim by relative path and passed against the source while the binary
shipped a stale copy. `tests/libsignal-shim.test.ts` imports it by PACKAGE NAME now, so
a stale copy is a red suite rather than a silent wrong binary.
See docs/rfc/PLAN_REPLACE_LIBSIGNAL.md in the parent repository.
